name: cli-adapter-registry
purpose: Defines how the installable platform can use many external CLIs without becoming dependent on any single CLI, vendor, shell, or developer environment.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before adding, invoking, bundling, or depending on a command-line tool from the platform, desktop app, monitor, or agent workflows.
how_to_read: Read platform_principle first: the platform is installable, but CLI tools are optional attached capabilities.
Read integration_layers to understand which layer owns UI, platform logic, adapter contracts, and external CLI execution.
Read structure_rules before adding a CLI so a missing tool degrades gracefully instead of breaking the platform.
Read cli_adapter_contract and execution_contract before designing a concrete adapter.
Read installation_policy before installing or bundling a CLI dependency.
update_triggers: A new CLI capability is added to the platform or desktop app.
A CLI is promoted from optional local tool to required dependency.
The platform starts invoking CLIs from a desktop shell, local service, or web monitor action.
Command execution security, allowlist, timeout, logging, output parsing, or secret redaction rules change.
A CLI provider, package manager, deployment tool, AI assistant CLI, or document conversion tool becomes a supported adapter.

structure_rules.rule: The installed platform must not require a specific external CLI just to open, browse history, view docs, or understand project state.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants an installable platform that can use CLIs on top of it, not a wrapper that breaks when one CLI is missing.

structure_rules.rule: Treat each CLI as an attached capability behind an adapter contract with availability checks, version checks, permission scope, output contract, and fallback behavior.
structure_rules.reason: Loose coupling keeps the platform usable across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, package managers, deployment tools, and future CLIs.

structure_rules.rule: Platform workflows should express intent and output contracts; CLI adapters translate that intent into provider-specific commands.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should orchestrate reusable work, while concrete CLIs remain replaceable implementation details.

structure_rules.rule: Prefer argv-style command invocation, explicit cwd, timeout, environment allowlist, and structured stdout/stderr handling. Avoid shell strings unless there is a recorded reason and escaping plan.
structure_rules.reason: Shell strings increase portability and injection risks, especially when user or repository data becomes command input.

structure_rules.rule: If the installable desktop shell invokes local commands, the allowed commands, arguments, workspace paths, and permission scope must be explicit before release.
structure_rules.reason: A desktop app has a stronger local-security boundary than a developer terminal session.

structure_rules.rule: A missing optional CLI should produce a human-readable capability_missing result with setup guidance, not crash the whole platform.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should remain useful even when optional toolchains are absent.

structure_rules.rule: Before a CLI becomes required, bundled, auto-installed, or globally configured, create an installation audit plan and rollback path.
structure_rules.reason: A required CLI changes dependency state and user environment expectations.

field_guide.meaning: The core statement that the platform is installable but CLI-neutral.
Layered ownership boundaries from installed shell to platform core to external CLI.
Rules that decide whether a CLI is optional, supported, required, bundled, or explicitly not supported.
Minimum fields a concrete CLI adapter must define before implementation.
Command execution rules for safety, portability, logging, timeouts, and output handling.
How the platform behaves when a CLI is unavailable, unsupported, times out, or returns unexpected output.

platform_principle.summary: The platform is installable and user-facing, but it is not locked to one CLI. It provides the durable workspace, UI, history, policies, and orchestration layer, then uses external CLIs through replaceable adapters when they are useful.
non_goals: becoming a thin wrapper around one AI assistant CLI
requiring every user to install developer CLIs before opening the app
embedding secrets or user-specific tool sessions into distributable builds
hard-coding shell commands in prompts instead of adapter contracts

owns: requirements, specs, history, evaluations, and navigation
must_not_own: vendor-specific command quirks unless isolated in an adapter

dependency_posture.promotion_rule: Promote a CLI from optional_supported to project_local_required or bundled_sidecar only after requirements, security review, installation audit, fallback plan, and validation commands exist.
dependency_posture.degradation_rule: If an optional CLI is missing, return capability_missing with setup instructions and continue all unrelated platform features.

cli_adapter_contract.storage_rule: Store shared adapter definitions under agent-platform/configs/integrations/ or project-specific configs/integrations/ when the adapter belongs to one project.

execution_contract.environment_policy: Pass only allowlisted environment variables. Never log secret values.
execution_contract.logging_policy: Record command intent, adapter id, version, duration, exit status, and redacted stderr. Do not store raw secrets or oversized outputs.
execution_contract.desktop_policy: Desktop-originated command execution must be scoped by command allowlist, workspace path allowlist, and user-visible permission settings.

capability_classes.notes: Assistant CLIs are execution providers, not the platform source of truth.
Git history can enrich the platform, but repository documents remain readable without GitHub-specific tooling.
Package manager use follows installation audit rules when it changes dependency or environment state.
Deployment CLIs require explicit target, credentials boundary, dry-run or preview path, and rollback notes.
Conversion tools should have deterministic input/output paths and preserve source provenance.

adapter_selection.tie_breaker: Prefer the adapter that requires the least new installation and leaves the clearest verification record.

failure_behavior.missing_cli: Return capability_missing with adapter_id, missing command, setup doc path, and safe next action.
failure_behavior.unsupported_version: Return capability_blocked with installed version, supported range if known, and upgrade or fallback guidance.
failure_behavior.timeout: Return command_timeout with duration, adapter_id, and partial output summary if safe.
failure_behavior.unexpected_output: Return output_contract_failed and preserve redacted sample output for debugging.
failure_behavior.permission_denied: Return permission_required and ask for explicit user approval or settings change.

installation_policy.global_install_rule: Avoid global install. If global install is necessary, record why project-local or tool-local is insufficient and document removal.
audit_required_when: CLI is bundled in an installer
authentication helper or credential store integration is added
